goal: Convert a Roman numeral string to an integer, rejecting invalid numerals
assumptions: Input is a string containing only characters from the set {'I','V','X','L','C','D','M'} for valid numerals; invalid numerals (e.g. 'IIII', 'VV', 'IC', 'IL', 'XD', 'XM', 'VX', 'LC', 'DM', empty string) must be rejected by raising a ValueError.

The function must reject invalid Roman numerals according to standard subtractive notation rules: only I, X, C can be used as subtractive prefixes; I can precede V and X only; X can precede L and C only; C can precede D and M only; no more than one smaller numeral before a larger one; no more than three consecutive identical numerals for I, X, C, M; V, L, D cannot be repeated.
The input string may be empty, in which case it is invalid and must raise ValueError.
The function is case-sensitive: only uppercase Roman numeral characters are valid; lowercase letters are invalid and must raise ValueError.
The return type is an integer.
The function must handle the full range of Roman numerals from 1 to 3999 inclusive; numerals representing values outside this range are invalid and must raise ValueError.
Whitespace or leading/trailing spaces are not stripped; any whitespace makes the input invalid and must raise ValueError.
The function must not accept non-string inputs; if a non-string is passed, it should raise a TypeError (natural Python behavior for string operations).

from solution import roman_to_int
import pytest


def test_basic_numerals():
    assert roman_to_int('I') == 1
    assert roman_to_int('V') == 5
    assert roman_to_int('X') == 10
    assert roman_to_int('L') == 50
    assert roman_to_int('C') == 100
    assert roman_to_int('D') == 500
    assert roman_to_int('M') == 1000


def test_additive_notation():
    assert roman_to_int('III') == 3
    assert roman_to_int('VII') == 7
    assert roman_to_int('XII') == 12
    assert roman_to_int('XXVII') == 27
    assert roman_to_int('MDCLXVI') == 1666


def test_subtractive_notation():
    assert roman_to_int('IV') == 4
    assert roman_to_int('IX') == 9
    assert roman_to_int('XL') == 40
    assert roman_to_int('XC') == 90
    assert roman_to_int('CD') == 400
    assert roman_to_int('CM') == 900


def test_combined_notation():
    assert roman_to_int('XIV') == 14
    assert roman_to_int('XIX') == 19
    assert roman_to_int('XLIV') == 44
    assert roman_to_int('XCIV') == 94
    assert roman_to_int('CDXLIV') == 444
    assert roman_to_int('CMXCIX') == 999
    assert roman_to_int('MCMXCIV') == 1994
    assert roman_to_int('MMXXIV') == 2024


def test_boundary_values():
    assert roman_to_int('I') == 1
    assert roman_to_int('MMMCMXCIX') == 3999

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
